facets.label: soft/flexible substrate or carrier
facets.description: Flexible carrier films, elastomers, paper/textile carriers, and substrate mechanics.

facets.label: electrodes, interconnects, conductive traces
facets.description: Conductive layers and connection features used to route or transduce signals.

facets.label: active/selective sensing material
facets.description: Materials whose chemistry or nanostructure creates sensitivity or selectivity.

facets.label: sensor/transducer core
facets.description: Actual sensing/transduction element: gas, electrochemical, optical, FET, pressure, strain, etc.

facets.label: microfluidic/gas path/chamber
facets.description: Chambers, channels, reservoirs, manifolds, standoff volumes, and sampling paths.

facets.label: optical/photonic module
facets.description: Light sources, waveguides, lenses, fibers, gratings, and optical readout elements.

facets.label: packaging/encapsulation/barrier
facets.description: Moisture, biofluid, splash, and mechanical protection around the working parts.

facets.label: body/tissue/environment interface and seal
facets.description: Device-to-body coupling: skin, wound, dressing, adhesive, gasket, or sterile interface.

facets.label: mechanical/stretchable structure
facets.description: Mechanical forms that preserve function under bending, strain, adhesion, or deployment.

facets.label: controller/flexible PCB/readout electronics
facets.description: Control, data acquisition, signal conditioning, flexible PCB, and integrated electronics.

facets.label: actuation/valve/pump/flow control
facets.description: Valves, pumps, electrowetting, magnetic or pneumatic actuation, and flow control.

facets.label: power/energy module
facets.description: Battery, wireless power, harvesters, capacitors, and power management.

facets.label: wireless/readout link
facets.description: Bluetooth, NFC, RF telemetry, reader/smartphone interfaces, and antennas.

facets.label: thermal/heater module
facets.description: Heaters, thermistors, heat-flux modules, and temperature-control elements.

facets.label: calibration/reference/truth block
facets.description: Reference channels, blank tests, calibration gas/liquid standards, and external truth methods.

facets.label: disposable/reusable cartridge split
facets.description: Separable disposable gas path, replaceable cartridge, reusable cap, or sterilization logic.

facets.label: therapy/delivery payload
facets.description: Drug delivery, stimulation, heating, antimicrobial, or therapeutic output blocks.

facets.label: printing/transfer/stamping patterning
facets.description: Pattern transfer by printing, stamping, transfer printing, or roll processes.

facets.label: lithography/etching/cleanroom patterning
facets.description: Photolithography, resist, etching, plasma, and cleanroom pattern definition.

facets.label: soft lithography/molding/casting
facets.description: PDMS molding, replica molding, embossing, casting, and 3D printed molds.

facets.label: thin-film deposition/coating
facets.description: Evaporation, sputtering, CVD, spin coating, electrodeposition, and film growth.

facets.label: lamination/bonding/stack assembly
facets.description: Layer alignment, bonding, lamination, packaging, and stack assembly.

facets.label: laser/thermal processing
facets.description: Laser ablation/transfer, thermal processing, annealing, and sintering.

nodes.label: Actuation, Therapy, and Delivery
nodes.description: Functions whose primary purpose is to generate controlled physical, chemical, optical, electrical, biological, or therapeutic intervention or to deliver an active payload.

nodes.label: Communication and Data Transfer
nodes.description: Functions that transmit, receive, address, multiplex, identify, synchronize, store for transfer, or remotely interrogate information between system components or locations.

nodes.label: Computing, Control, and Decision Support
nodes.description: Digital or algorithmic functions that transform acquired data into features, estimates, classifications, decisions, feedback, scheduling, or intervention commands.

nodes.label: Electronics and Signal Conditioning
nodes.description: Electronic components and front-end circuits that bias, amplify, filter, multiplex, buffer, rectify, switch, condition, or route signals before higher-level computation or communication.

nodes.label: Fabrication and Assembly
nodes.description: Processes and assembly operations whose primary purpose is to create, pattern, release, transfer, align, replicate, or integrate material and device structures.

nodes.label: Modeling, Calibration, Validation, and Translation
nodes.description: Reusable methods for calibrating measurements, constructing or inverting models, validating mechanisms and performance, quantifying uncertainty, and assessing translation or application readiness.

nodes.label: Packaging, Deployment, and Lifecycle
nodes.description: Functions that protect, package, deploy, fix, conform, retrieve, reuse, biodegrade, resorb, or otherwise govern a device's operational environment and lifecycle.

nodes.label: Power and Energy
nodes.description: Functions that generate, harvest, convert, store, regulate, buffer, distribute, or thermally manage energy for system operation.

nodes.label: Sample Acquisition, Transport, and Fluidics
nodes.description: Functions that acquire, contain, condition, route, mix, separate, store, recover, or deliver fluids and samples through physical fluidic pathways.

nodes.label: Sensing, Transduction, Imaging, and Output
nodes.description: Functions that convert physical, chemical, biological, optical, or mechanical inputs into measured, imaged, indicated, or otherwise observable outputs.

nodes.label: Structures, Materials, and Interfaces
nodes.description: Reusable physical architectures, material behaviors, and interfaces that define mechanical, optical, electrical, chemical, biological, or transport boundary conditions independent of a specific fabrication step.

nodes.label: 3D Deformation-Amplified Pressure Transduction
nodes.description: Use compliant three-dimensional structures in which applied pressure deforms the structure, increases strain in integrated gauges, and changes their electrical resistance.
nodes.function: Measure or enhance local normal-pressure transduction in compliant interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Pressure deforms cavities, pillars, suspended membranes, or tent-like mesostructures, concentrating displacement or strain in an electrical transducer.
preconditions: The transducer can couple to deformation, displacement, or strain.

nodes.label: 3D Electrolyte-Access Electrode Architecture
nodes.description: Use an open, interconnected 3D electrode architecture with thin active layers to shorten ion-transport paths while retaining electronic connectivity.
nodes.function: Improve rate capability and preserve high active-material utilization in high-surface-area electrodes.
nodes.mechanism: Interconnected pores and walls expose internal active surfaces to electrolyte while connected current collectors provide electronic pathways.
preconditions: electrolyte can access internal and external surfaces
structure remains connected to a current collector

nodes.label: 3D Multimodal Tissue Interface
nodes.description: Use a flexible three-dimensional electronic-tissue framework to colocate electrical and mechanical sensing at multiple defined locations and, in some implementations, provide electrical or pharmacological modulation.
nodes.function: Measure and perturb biological activity over a three-dimensional soft-tissue geometry.
nodes.mechanism: A shaped or compliant framework maintains tissue contact while electrical, mechanical, optical, thermal, chemical, or pharmacological channels operate with coordinated acquisition or control.
outputs: electrical, optical, thermal, or pharmacological modulation
preconditions: electronic and mechanical channels must share timing
tissue geometry must be compatible with the support layout
failure_modes: loading conditions that do not represent the intended physiology

nodes.label: Active Array Readout
nodes.description: Use local switches or buffers with sequential row and shared-column addressing to connect many distributed sensor sites to a smaller set of readout lines.
nodes.function: Reduce wiring and external acquisition burden while preserving access to dense sensor arrays.
nodes.mechanism: Row selection activates local unit cells; switches and optional local amplifiers route selected signals to shared column outputs.
outputs: selected and optionally amplified pixel outputs
preconditions: Array elements can be electrically addressed
Readout timing and channel addressing are coordinated.
Switching and readout electronics are mechanically compatible with the substrate
electrode pairs are physically isolated or sufficiently decoupled
pixel transistors remain electrically isolated from fluid
pixels can integrate switches or transistors
row and column routing is available
failure_modes: Switching limited by control slew rate

nodes.label: Actuation-Coupled Modulus Sensing
nodes.description: Estimate local soft-tissue modulus by mechanically coupling an actuating element to one or more sensing elements and calibrating the electrical response against tissue mechanics.
nodes.function: Measure local stiffness or elastic modulus on compliant or curved biological surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Periodic actuation deforms the substrate and contacting tissue; coupled sensors measure the resulting response, which is mapped to modulus by a calibration model.
preconditions: actuator and sensor are mechanically coupled through tissue or substrate
calibration or model relating voltage to modulus is available
probe maintains contact with the target tissue
failure_modes: non-monotonic response at high or low modulus
reduced deformation and signal with overly stiff substrate

nodes.label: Adhesion-Bounded Relief Operating Window
nodes.description: Choose relief geometry, stiffness, adhesion, and preload within lower and upper bounds that support reversible collapse and reliable pickup or release.
nodes.function: Translate mechanics and interface parameters into a stable operating window for compliant transfer structures.
nodes.mechanism: The lower bound ensures elastic recovery overcomes adhesion after collapse; the upper bound limits restoring-force-driven delamination or self-collapse through energy balance.
preconditions: Backing-layer deformation is negligible or separately bounded
Known interface adhesion and elastic properties
Scale behaves approximately as a beam

nodes.label: Adhesion-Driven Conformal Contact
nodes.description: Use a sufficiently compliant thin device and interfacial adhesion or capillary energy to establish passive, conformal contact with a curved or textured surface.
nodes.function: Create low-force, intimate, and potentially reversible device-surface contact.
nodes.mechanism: Interfacial adhesion, van der Waals forces, or drying-induced capillary forces overcome the bending-energy penalty of a compliant film.
preconditions: Tissue curvature within the conformal-contact range
adequate interfacial adhesion or residual bonding
adhesion energy exceeds geometry-dependent critical threshold
failure_modes: Poor contact on extreme curvature or hair

nodes.function: Place fragile functional materials on selected substrates while preserving pattern and registration.

Receiving surface has favorable surface-energy contrast
Stamp adhesion can be reversibly modulated
Stamp can conform to the donor and receiver.
Substrate chemistry can form a stronger bond to the film than the stamp does.
bonding between transferred metal and substrate interface
film remains mechanically continuous during release
network density is sufficient for percolation

receiver adhesion becomes stronger after curing

receiver-film adhesion can exceed stamp-film adhesion
stamp and receiver adhesion can be sequenced

Reduced coverage uniformity from stamp relief disrupting flow alignment
poor transfer to low-energy or rough substrates

nodes.label: Adhesion–Elasticity Collapse Modeling
nodes.description: Predict equilibrium collapse, contact extent, and stability of compliant relief structures by minimizing elastic deformation energy minus adhesion-energy gain.
nodes.function: Relate relief geometry and material/interface properties to collapse onset, extent, and stability.
nodes.mechanism: A continuum or equivalent-crack representation computes deformation energy and subtracts adhesion energy over the contacting region; total-energy minimization determines the state.
preconditions: Adhesion and deformation energies can be represented in a continuum model
Compliant relief structure contacting a relatively rigid surface
fracture-mechanics or elastic-energy representation is applicable
interface adhesion can be represented by an effective energy
failure_modes: Incorrect prediction if material nonlinearities or kinetics dominate
Model invalid when collapse length exceeds post spacing
model assumptions violated by non-cylindrical patterns
poor transfer of calibrated parameter across geometries

nodes.label: Behavioral Validation of Biointerventions
nodes.description: Use controlled behavioral assays, matched controls, and performance-versus-chance or condition comparisons to validate perceptual, analgesic, functional, or deployment effects of a biointervention.
nodes.function: Establish organism-level detectability, efficacy, and behavioral artifacts.
nodes.mechanism: Intervention state is paired with evoked behavior, preference, discrimination, mobility, social, or task-performance measurements under controlled comparison conditions.
preconditions: Animal can perform the operant task
failure_modes: inability to directly measure subjective pain

nodes.label: Bending-Dominated Resonance Scaling
nodes.description: Use FEA to determine shape- and mode-dependent scaling factors in bending-dominated vibration modeling.
nodes.function: Guide resonator design across material systems and geometric scales.
nodes.mechanism: Relate effective bending stiffness and mass to frequency through dimensionless shape or mode factors, with calibration from FEA or experiment when needed.
outputs: Scaled geometry for a target frequency range
preconditions: shape factor is known or calibrated

nodes.label: Bias-Controlled Ionic Barrier Protection
nodes.description: Control or suppress bias-driven ionic transport through an insulating barrier to stabilize an underlying electronic device in an ionic environment.
nodes.function: Explain and manage bias-induced ionic degradation and threshold drift.
nodes.mechanism: An applied electric field drives mobile ions toward or through the barrier; barrier composition and thickness regulate transport and charge accumulation near the active interface.
outputs: reduced ion concentration at the device
preconditions: capping layers with sufficiently low ionic diffusivity
charged mobile species in surrounding fluid

nodes.label: Bilayer Mismatch-Deformation Modeling
nodes.description: Model or characterize bonded-bilayer bending and rolling angle from mismatch/prestrain and layer thickness or thickness ratio using analytic or finite-element approaches.
nodes.function: Translate layer mismatch and geometry into designed bilayer shape change.
nodes.mechanism: Represent differential expansion or contraction as eigenstrain or equivalent thermal strain, then enforce layered stress and moment equilibrium or solve nonlinear shell/solid mechanics.
preconditions: small enough prestrain for the stated kinematic assumption
failure_modes: model mismatch outside assumed constitutive or geometric regime

nodes.label: Biofluid Conditioning and Antifouling Routing
nodes.description: Condition or route sweat before sensing to remove serum-soluble interferents and refresh the sensing site, improving measurement accuracy.
nodes.function: Improve sample quality and analytical accuracy before or during measurement.
nodes.mechanism: Preconcentration, incubation, selective barriers, hydrogel interfaces, refreshed sensing zones, or channel routing separate target fluid from interferents.
preconditions: processing time and volume are compatible with use

nodes.label: Biofluid-Barrier Encapsulation
nodes.description: Encapsulate functional electronics with one or more conformal barrier layers that limit water, ion, or biofluid ingress while preserving operation in the intended environment.
nodes.function: Protect electronics from fluid-induced leakage, corrosion, degradation, and mechanical exposure.

inputs: front and back thermally grown SiO2 layers

Encapsulation adheres continuously to the assembled device
Layer properties are compatible with the intended lifetime
The barrier remains continuous during bending
barrier layers covering the active structure
barrier materials compatible with the deployment environment
coating is continuous over exposed regions
compatibility with optical and electrical interfaces
continuous coverage of front and back surfaces
encapsulant compatibility with optical sensing window
encapsulant is compatible with components and wireless operation

no required external ports or mechanical switches
oxide layers remain continuous and defect-poor
the stimulus does not require direct exposure of the protected sensing material

nodes.label: Biofluid-Barrier Lifetime Validation
nodes.description: Expose encapsulated structures to defined PBS conditions and monitor electrical performance over the soak period to assess barrier stability.
nodes.function: Quantify barrier survival and identify failure onset.
nodes.mechanism: Fluid ingress or barrier degradation alters a measurable protected structure response; comparison with an unprotected control estimates the protection interval.

Device response is measurable before and after exposure
failure_modes: False lifetime attribution from reader-medium changes

nodes.label: Bioresorbable Implanted Physiological Sensing
nodes.description: Use a bioresorbable implanted sensor whose barrier thickness and material hydrolysis determine its functional lifetime, with physiological-timescale lifetime estimated from accelerated testing.
nodes.function: Measure physiological variables during a defined implant interval and then resorb.
nodes.mechanism: A transient sensor combines a physiological transducer with dissolution-rate control and an external or optical readout interface.
aliases: transient implanted pressure and temperature sensing

nodes.label: BLE Wireless Monitoring Link
nodes.description: Transmit measurements autonomously or wirelessly via Bluetooth Low Energy from wearable or skin-mounted sensing systems to smartphones or other external interfaces.
nodes.function: Provide low-duty-cycle wireless monitoring and remote readout.
nodes.mechanism: A BLE radio or system-on-chip advertises or connects to a receiving interface and transports digitized sensor data.
preconditions: A compatible wireless receiver or phone interface is required.
Implanted module remains mechanically and fluidically protected
Sensing and storage must operate within the available power budget.
Wireless link is within operating range
listener can scan and recognize the device ID

nodes.label: Bonding-Pattern and Prestrain 2D-to-3D Programming
nodes.description: Program thin-film or ribbon 3D geometry by jointly selecting planar precursor layout, selective bonding pattern, and substrate prestrain.
nodes.function: Translate planar layout and assembly loading into a target buckled, folded, or otherwise transformed 3D architecture.
nodes.mechanism: Bonding sites constrain motion and delimit released regions; precursor geometry selects deformation modes; prestrain supplies compressive displacement and amplitude.
outputs: Spatially varying buckle width and amplitude
controlled curvature, pitch, chirality, elevation, or nesting
preconditions: Adhesion sites are registered to the ribbon
Prestrain is above the buckling threshold
The ribbon can separate from weakly bonded regions
a mechanically characterized precursor and substrate
adhesion can be selectively activated or suppressed
geometry is within the assembly process window
mechanical response remains elastic or otherwise recoverable
interfaces: Mechanical boundary conditions at adhesion sites
failure_modes: Cracking from overly narrow inactive regions
Very long inactivated regions causing short-wave modes

nodes.label: Capacitive Biointerface Through Barrier
nodes.description: Use a high-impedance or thin capping layer to protect electronics from biofluids and enable tissue or fluid interface measurements, with shielding used to reduce environmental coupling where demonstrated.
nodes.function: Record or stimulate biological potentials or measure nearby fluid while protecting electronics and reducing parasitic signals.
nodes.mechanism: Signals couple capacitively through a controlled dielectric barrier; barrier thickness and conductive shielding set desired and parasitic coupling.
preconditions: Background coupling is a significant error source
Fluid and electrodes can be separated by a controlled dielectric

nodes.label: Catalyst-Free Direct Nanowire Heteroepitaxy
nodes.description: Directly grow compositionally tunable one-dimensional semiconductor nanowire arrays on a crystalline or conducting substrate without metal catalyst particles or prepatterning.
nodes.function: Create ordered heterogeneous nanowire arrays integrated directly with a substrate.
nodes.mechanism: MOCVD enables direct epitaxial or mismatch-strain-driven self-assembly; nanowire geometry laterally relaxes lattice mismatch, while substrate, diameter, and growth conditions control coherence and yield.
preconditions: Growth conditions supporting direct epitaxial nucleation
Growth conditions within the nanowire heteroepitaxy window
failure_modes: Irregular nanoneedles or islands above the critical diameter

nodes.label: Chemical Carrier-Polarity Control
nodes.description: Change the carrier polarity of a semiconducting channel through chemically induced charge transfer or doping, optionally with spatially selective coating.
nodes.function: Configure p-type, n-type, or ambipolar operation without changing the basic electrode layout.
nodes.mechanism: A chemically active coating, electrolyte, or dielectric transfers charge or alters injection at the semiconductor surface, shifting carrier polarity and threshold behavior.
preconditions: chemical groups must interact electronically with the channel
chemically accessible nanotube or contact regions
coating is chemically compatible with the dielectric and channel

nodes.label: Chemical Surface-Directed BCP Assembly
nodes.description: Use spatially patterned surface chemistry and differential wetting to register and orient self-assembled block-copolymer domains.
nodes.function: Direct BCP domain orientation and spatial registration.
nodes.mechanism: Block-selective or neutral surface interactions alter interfacial free energy and guide domain morphology at designated regions.
preconditions: Surface chemistry can be patterned at or below the BCP feature scale
chemical pattern period is compatible with BCP natural period

nodes.label: Chemically Selective Contact Transfer
nodes.description: Transfer patterned solid material by conformal contact and selective chemical bonding that makes substrate–ink adhesion exceed ink–stamp adhesion.
nodes.function: Patterned material transfer with spatial selectivity.
nodes.mechanism: Conformal contact brings reactive interfaces together; patterned or uniform surface chemistry creates stronger bonding at selected substrate regions, and stamp removal leaves the material transferred.
preconditions: Reactive donor and receiver interfaces are available
substrate–ink bonding stronger than ink–stamp adhesion

nodes.label: Closed-Loop Bioelectronic Modulation
nodes.description: Sense biological state, infer a condition, and conditionally trigger or adjust a bioelectronic therapeutic actuator.
nodes.function: Provide state-dependent real-time biological intervention.
nodes.mechanism: Physiological sensors feed signal processing or inference; decision logic controls electrical, optical, thermal, or pharmacological actuation through local or wireless interfaces.

nodes.label: Closed-Loop Thermal Regulation
nodes.description: Regulate a local thermal actuator using temperature feedback and a controller to track a target temperature or thermal state.
nodes.function: Deliver repeatable thermal exposure while limiting overshoot and damage.
nodes.mechanism: A temperature sensor measures the actuator or target; a controller modulates heater power, duty cycle, or drive current against a set point.
outputs: Thermal stimulus with monitored set point

Temperature response must be measurable and controllable
heater and sensor are thermally coupled
heater and temperature sensor are co-located or thermally coupled
temperature measurement remains interpretable during stimulation

nodes.label: Co-Registered Multimodal Biointerface
nodes.description: Integrate multiple sensing and actuation modalities on compliant or flexible biological interfaces for simultaneous recording and modulation.
nodes.function: Measure, stimulate, perturb, and monitor biological systems across multiple physical modalities.
nodes.mechanism: Electrical, optical, thermal, chemical, mechanical, or fluidic modules share a tissue-conforming substrate or three-dimensional framework while retaining modality-specific addressing.
inputs: chemical, optical, thermal, or mechanical stimuli
electrical, optical, thermal, and chemical modules
preconditions: Modules must be electrically and mechanically compatible
The platform must maintain soft tissue proximity
Thermal and optical loads must be controlled

nodes.label: Colorimetric Chemical Readout
nodes.description: Convert analyte-dependent color changes into quantitative chemical estimates using calibrated optical or digital color measurements.
nodes.function: Provide low-complexity optical quantification of chemical analytes.

Optical contrast is sufficient for imaging
